\opt{B}{3}
\opt{C}{6}
\opt{D}{5}

\begin{bankq}[id=SI11-P1-MATH-S2-Q07, source={Score-I - Test 11 (27 Feb 2022)}, paper=1, qno=7, type=multi, subtopic={Differentiability of modulus and greatest-integer functions}, answer={A,C}, answer_src=key, difficulty=7, diff_parts={K2 S2 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: differentiability, a product with an arbitrary function at x = 1 | steps: f has a factor (x - 1) near 1 so f(1) = 0; check derivative of product via limit; continuity of g needed; test each statement | I: f(1) = 0 and f'(1) = 0 behaviours}, also_in={JEE Advanced (2021 Series) - Test 02 (04 Feb 2021) P1 Q7}]
Let the function $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be defined by $f(x)=x^3-x^2+(x-1)\sin x$ and let $g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be an arbitrary function. Let $fg:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be the product function defined by $(fg)(x)=f(x)g(x)$. Then which of the following statements is/are TRUE ?
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{If $g$ is continuous at $x=1$, then $fg$ is differentiable at $x=1$}
\opt{B}{If $fg$ is differentiable at $x=1$, then $g$ is continuous at $x=1$}
\opt{C}{If $g$ is differentiable at $x=1$, then $fg$ is differentiable at $x=1$}
\opt{D}{If $fg$ is differentiable at $x=1$, then $g$ is differentiable at $x=1$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
